newsitem.title: USA: N.J. lowers average workers' comp premiums 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: N.J. lowers average workers' comp premiums 11 pct.

text.p: Premiums paid by New Jersey employers for workers' compensation insurance will fall an average of 11.2 percent beginning next year, Gov. Christine Whitman said Friday.
About 169,000 businesses in the state will see savings of about $218 million as a result of the drop, Whitman said in a news release.

"The smallest to the largest companies in the state will experience this premium savings, from a modest $50 premium savings to tens of thousands of dollars for the largest premium payers," Whitman said.
New Jersey's Compensation Rating and Inspection Bureau recommended the rate decrease based on improved loss ratios, which compare losses to premiums.
The state attributed the better loss performance to workplace safety efforts, increased use of managed care, and higher employment rates.
Gualberto Medina, New Jersey's commissioner of commerce and economic development, said workers' compensation premium rates are a key determinant of where companies choose to locate.
